title: Choose the public website's design
question: Round 3, still clean and standard: three more ways to organise the page. Pick one, or steer another round.

options.label: Bento
options.lineage: modern product sites built from bento-grid tiles
options.thesis: The overview as a tidy grid of tiles: next game, latest result, coming up, standings and leaders at a glance.
options.viewport: Light grey ground, header row with season, division and tabs, then a five-tile grid led by an orange next-game tile.
options.risk: Tiles stack into a long list on phones; tile sizes must stay consistent across pages.

options.label: Focus
options.lineage: calm single-column reading sites and mobile apps
options.thesis: One centred column: league, next game, results and standings in reading order, identical on phone and desktop.
options.viewport: Breadcrumb, large league title, tabs, division switch, next-game panel, then recent results and a short standings list.
options.risk: Leaves wide screens mostly empty; full tables live on their own tabs.

options.label: Stats Hub
options.lineage: reference sites such as Basketball-Reference, modernised
options.thesis: Data first: a dense, sortable standings table with every column, quick facts and an on-this-page index.
options.viewport: Slim dark bar, league header with quick facts, sub-tabs, a left on-this-page index, the full standings table, then results and upcoming tables.
options.risk: Dense for casual visitors on phones; best for fans who want every number.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A pro-league site as NBA.com, EuroLeague or the PBA site would ship it, done with full care.
canonCard.viewport: Scores strip across the top, navy navigation, league header with tabs, next game and results beside standings.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every league site by design; least Shotclock-specific.
